build.summary: I split src/simulation/angioPci.ts (1,818 lines) into src/simulation/pci/state.ts and 13 action modules under src/simulation/pci/actions/. angioPci.ts is now a facade. It re-exports the public symbols of state.ts by name and everything else with `export *` from each action module, so it exports the same 77 runtime names and 19 type names as before. Behaviour is unchanged. Before the split I recorded a scripted run of all four scenarios: wiring, torque, a guide extension and buddy wire, the full device workflow with the supervised ACT gate, timed inflations including melon-seeding and a burst, scoring, IVL and covered-stent passes, compatibility-path stent and post-dilatation, every drug and bail-out, IVUS pullback, the pressure wire (equalise, measure, pullback, drift check), debrief and metrics. Its 752,311-byte JSON output is byte-identical after the split (sha256 c09c0301…). Two helpers are needed by a second action module: handleWireEvents (wire.ts, used by devices.ts) and rupture/applyInflation (inflation.ts, used by step.ts). Each sits in its module's default export, which `export *` does not pass on, so neither leaks into the facade. The shared helpers in state.ts (log, tele, withNotes, syncWire, wireOf, syncMirrors, specOf, refDAt, lesionCover, lesionShape) are not re-exported either. loadDevice, moveDevice, inflate and deflate are marked @deprecated with a note that pci-lab-shell-session removes their UI callers; headless tests still use them. bailouts.ts is an empty module (`export {}`) with a header for the later bail-out packages.

build.notes:
The snapshot is at datasets/tmp/wp-snapshots/pci-engine-modularise/: src/simulation/angioPci.ts (the only listed file that already existed) and .started. Every other listed file is new.

Two departures from the design text:
1. The plan's design names 'initPci'; the existing function is initialPci, and I kept that name so the export list stays frozen.
2. The design says angioPci.ts becomes 'export * from these plus the existing type re-exports'. Doing that for state.ts too would leak its internal helpers into the facade, so state.ts is re-exported by name and only the action modules use `export *`. New public functions added to an action module still reach the facade without editing angioPci.ts; none of the later packages lists angioPci.ts.

Two helpers are shared between action modules, and each module puts them in a default-exported object (wireInternal in wire.ts, inflationInternal in inflation.ts). This keeps them out of the facade because `export *` does not re-export default. bailouts.ts and the angioPci.ts header explain the convention.

Where things went:
- PciScenario is defined in state.ts (initialPci and lesionNow need it, and state.ts may not import an action module); scenario.ts re-exports it as a type.
- The generic bailout() lives in drugs.ts beside giveDrug, which calls it, because the design asks for an empty bailouts.ts.
- inject and injectPci went to imaging.ts.
- cxContext went to step.ts.
- routeTurning went to assessment.ts.
- Geometry wrappers (pciGeom, sampleAtMm, routeSamples, takeOffAngle, routeEndMm) and lesionNow went to state.ts.
- DEFAULT_SHAPE, WIRE_SPEC, tipBend, pathToTarget and branchLabel went to wire.ts.
- guideBackupN went to guide.ts.
- deviceDiameterNow and deviceSpecOf went to devices.ts.
- lumenFor, pciPatientEffects and complicationsNow went to patient.ts.

Log and telemetry names and fields are unchanged; the fingerprint compares full event and telemetry arrays. No dose, threshold or device value was added or changed. Every moved literal is copied verbatim, and the existing MODEL PARAMETER labels (MP_MELON_*, the extension inflow fraction) are kept. I did not touch the browser or the dev server.

review.verdict: ACCEPT, with one cross-package fix needed before later packages run. The refactor is behaviour-preserving, and I checked that myself. I parsed the snapshot of src/simulation/angioPci.ts and every new file with the TypeScript compiler API and compared each top-level declaration after normalising whitespace. Every declaration is verbatim apart from two call sites: advanceDevice now calls wireInternal.handleWireEvents and stepPci now calls inflationInternal.rupture. The only new declarations are the two default-exported helper objects. Nothing is missing or duplicated, and no module-level mutable state was split. The original's static runtime export list (77 names) matches FROZEN in facade.test.ts exactly. The 19 type names (WireKind, BalloonKind, PciGeom, TipShape, PciScenario, DeviceKind, DeviceStage, Device, Placed, PciEvent, PciTelemetry, PciState, InitOptions, AdvanceOptions, StepOptions, PciDrug, PciMetricsReport, PciDebrief, RngState) are all still exported. tsconfig.app.json includes test files, so the type-import test is really checked by tsc. Tests I ran: facade + angioPci + complications gave 3 files, 32 tests passed; the 7 existing src/simulation/pci/*.test.ts files gave 43 tests passed; tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit is clean. The running Vite server on 5173 returns 200 for angioPci.ts, state.ts and all 13 action modules. state.ts imports no action module. The action-module graph has no cycle, and the cycle test checks real edges, so it is not tautological. @deprecated markers are on loadDevice, moveDevice, inflate and deflate. Log and telemetry calls are unchanged, so tip context is unaffected. No clinical numbers were added; the MP_MELON_* MODEL PARAMETER constants were moved verbatim. There are no UI, render-path or design-system changes, and the new comments use British English. Other files under src/ newer than .started (src/progress/*, src/mentor/skillCards.ts, src/mentor/debrief.ts, src/mentor/mentor.test.ts, src/mentor/registries.test.ts, src/ui/mentor/Debrief.tsx, src/ui/mentor/debrief/*) are listed by found-mentor-registries, progression-labels and progression-exams, or are new tests of those packages. They are not attributable to this package. Still open: the browser acceptance criterion (the PCI lab loads and window.__pciDraw() renders a frame) has not been verified in a browser. The browser stage has to confirm it.

findings.where: src/simulation/pci/facade.test.ts, tests 'Object.keys of the angioPci module equals the frozen pre-split list' and 'each export keeps its kind'
findings.problem: Both tests require exact equality with FROZEN (toEqual on the sorted key list and on the full kinds map). Later packages add public exports to action modules: pci-wire-microcatheter (wire.ts), pci-indeflator (inflation.ts), pci-perforation, pci-flow-closure and pci-acs-thrombus (bailouts.ts), pci-equipment-tray (devices.ts) and others. None of them lists facade.test.ts, so each will hit a failing test it is not allowed to edit. The builder raised this in outOfScope, but the test itself is this package's file.
findings.fix: After this package is accepted against the strict check, relax the two assertions to a superset check that still freezes the pre-split surface: `const keys = Object.keys(facade); expect(keys).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(Object.keys(FROZEN))); expect(keys).not.toContain("default"); for (const [k, t] of Object.entries(FROZEN)) expect(typeof (facade as Record<string, unknown>)[k], k).toBe(t);`. Keep the internal-helper exclusion test as it is. The alternative is for the planner to add src/simulation/pci/facade.test.ts to every later package that adds a public export, so each can extend FROZEN.

findings.problem: state.ts is re-exported by explicit name, not by `export *`, so its helpers stay private. That was the right call. The side effect is that a public type or function a later package adds to state.ts does not reach the facade unless angioPci.ts is edited. pci-equipment-tray, pci-indeflator, pci-device-delivery, pci-wire-microcatheter and pci-two-rail-engine all list state.ts, and none lists angioPci.ts.
findings.fix: Planner note for those packages: put new public types and functions in the relevant action module (which `export *` already passes on), or import them directly from src/simulation/pci/state, or add src/simulation/angioPci.ts to the package's file list. No code change is needed in this package.

findings.problem: applyInflation is placed in the shared internal object, but no other module uses it; only rupture is called from step.ts. The builder report says both are used by step.ts, which is inaccurate. This is harmless, but it widens the internal surface for no reason.
findings.fix: Change it to `const inflationInternal = { rupture };`. Optionally amend the doc comment above it to name rupture only.

rejected: Finding 2 (state.ts re-exported by name, so new public symbols added there do not reach the facade): verified and correct, but the reviewer itself says no code change is needed in this package. It is a planner note for pci-equipment-tray, pci-indeflator, pci-device-delivery, pci-wire-microcatheter and pci-two-rail-engine. Those packages should put new public symbols in an action module, import them from src/simulation/pci/state directly, or add src/simulation/angioPci.ts to their file list. I made no edit here.

I applied two of the three findings and rejected one, which needed only a planner note.

Finding 1 (major, applied). Two tests in /Users/qc25212/Downloads/Misc/Games and apps/Cath Simulator/src/simulation/pci/facade.test.ts demanded an exact match with the frozen pre-split list of exports. Any later package that adds a public export would break them, and none of those packages may edit this file. The strict version passed at build time, and the facade still exports exactly the 77 pre-split names. I relaxed both tests to a lower-bound check, as the reviewer suggested:

- The kind test now checks the typeof of each frozen name with the name as the failure message (`toBe(t)`).
I added a comment saying the facade may grow but must never lose a name. These tests are unchanged: the internal-helper exclusion test, the state.ts import test, the cycle test and the action-module list test.

In /Users/qc25212/Downloads/Misc/Games and apps/Cath Simulator/src/simulation/pci/actions/inflation.ts the shared internal object now holds only `rupture`: `const inflationInternal = { rupture };`. A grep found that step.ts is its only outside user and calls only `inflationInternal.rupture`, so the builder report was wrong to say step.ts also uses applyInflation. applyInflation stays a private function inside inflation.ts. I reworded the doc comment to name rupture only.
